source.title: A Black Box Made Less Opaque (part 2)

record.file_problem: None; the full post text is present. Figures are referenced but their graphics are not included in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports analyses of GPT-2 Small SAE features, not individual neurons or neuron polysemanticity as described in the claim versions. Its results are related but do not test those versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures SAE-feature specialization and aggregate activation geometry across text forms and topics. These are related to questions about representation, but are not measurements of neuron polysemanticity. Reported math-completion results do not bear on the claim.
record.test_reason: The post measures how pretrained residual-stream SAE features in GPT-2 Small respond to matched texts in different surface forms. It uses specialist scores, Jaccard overlap and cosine similarity. It never examines individual MLP neurons or image-classifier neurons, or whether any unit responds to unrelated inputs. Nor does it touch superposition as a cause, architecture effects or measurement dependence of neuron polysemanticity. No result bears on V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author concludes that the top specialist SAE features respond mainly to syntax (surface form), while the full 24,576-feature representation clusters by semantics (topic). He suggests a possible two-tier structure. H3 was inconclusive because GPT-2 Small could not do the math completions. He has low confidence that the findings transfer to modern models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained residual-stream SAEs with matched text forms and activation-similarity analyses; it does not apply a method for identifying or testing polysemantic neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: The post contrasts specialist-feature overlap with cosine similarity across all SAE features; it also reports that symbolic forms show specialization in earlier layers, without specifying layerwise values in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small layer 11, the top-5 specialist SAE features overlap little across surface forms of the same topic (mean Jaccard 0.13). Yet full SAE activation vectors are more similar within topic (cosine 0.50) than across topics (0.14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In GPT-2 Small, highly active SAE features are surface-form-specific while the aggregate SAE representation groups by topic. This is a feature-level result, not one about neuron polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: Math_Simple forms have similar specialist scores (33, 31, 29) but largely different top features (#7029 vs #4163).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Similar SAE specialist selectivity across forms need not reflect shared features.

record.problems: Uses GPT-2 Small, and the author says applicability to more modern models is uncertain. The specialist activation threshold of 5.0 was chosen somewhat arbitrarily. The post describes the cosine difference as statistically significant but gives no test details or uncertainty estimates. The full figures are not present in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The math-completion accuracy discussion was omitted because it does not measure neuron polysemanticity or any listed version. Figure-only details without values in the text were not extracted.

untested.parts: All of it: no vision models.
All of it: no MLP neurons examined, only residual-stream SAE features.
All of it: superposition is not tested.
All of it: no architecture or activation-function variation.
All of it: no canonical polysemantic neurons are re-examined.
All of it at neuron level. The arbitrary 5.0 activation threshold for SAE specialists is not varied.

record.verdict_notes: This is an amateur LessWrong replication-style post on SAE features. It is not peer reviewed. Figures are absent from the text. Nothing here concerns neuron polysemanticity, so the record's T6/discusses classification and none-links are appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Image-classifier neurons and mixed image inputs.
Transformer MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and layerwise prevalence.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity caused by initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Effects of activation function, architecture, or regularization on neuron polysemanticity and performance.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect one shared feature or related jobs when explained with better tools.
Whether a neuron’s polysemantic classification changes with activation range or explanation scoring.
